default.p.test-5-p1.vietnamese: Sisyphus is a character who appears in Greek mythology. Because he deceived the gods, he was sentenced to an endless punishment. He had to push a huge boulder to the top of a mountain, but the moment he finally rolled it into place, it would tumble back down. Although he had to continue performing a meaningless action with no purpose, even in that desperate situation Sisyphus found joy and hope in his own way. People hold the belief that "effort will always be rewarded" or that "effort never betrays us," and devote themselves wholeheartedly to working hard. Yet sometimes that effort comes to nothing, and sometimes everyday life simply repeats itself with no prospect of improvement. How should we overcome this? The answer may lie in the story of Sisyphus. Sisyphus teaches us that our fate is something we decide and build ourselves. The story tells us that whether our actions become nothing more than a waste of time or a new way of life depends entirely on us.

default.p.test-8-p1.outline.0.note: Summarizes education's role in providing useful knowledge for daily life, while schools pass on cultural and family values.
default.p.test-8-p1.outline.1.label: Classifying experience and its overlap with education
default.p.test-8-p1.outline.1.note: The passage classifies experience as direct or indirect and points out that indirect experience transmitted through language can also be considered a form of education. This provides evidence for Question 1.
default.p.test-8-p1.outline.2.label: The boundary between experience and education and a comparison of their value
default.p.test-8-p1.outline.2.note: Affirms that it is difficult to draw a clear boundary between experience and education, and that one cannot claim experience is more valuable than education in life.
default.p.test-8-p1.vietnamese: Through education, we acquire knowledge that is important and useful in life. Every society has several types of schools that teach us the values of the family and traditional society. On the other hand, experience can be divided into two types: one is direct and personal, while the other is indirect and impersonal, acquired through other people's experiences. We can regard this second type of experience as a form of education. The reason is that such experiences are conveyed to us primarily through language. Strictly speaking, it is difficult to draw a clear boundary between experience and education. In everyday life, we cannot definitely say that experience is more valuable than education.

default.q.test-20-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 一般の病院より安い。
According to the passage, this convenient clinic attracts patients with its main competitive advantage: “fast and cheap” (「早い、安い」を売り物に). Patients do not have to wait long and can spend less than they would at an ordinary hospital.
default.q.test-20-q1-1.explanation: The clearest basis for identifying the cause of the rapid expansion is the second sentence of the passage:「内科医による監督など簡単な規制しかなく、「早い、安い」を売り物に３〜４年前の数十から今では全米で１２００カ所とまたたく間に広まった。」A complete translation is: "With only simple regulations, such as supervision by internists, and promoting 'fast and inexpensive' service as its selling point, this model spread in the blink of an eye from several dozen locations three or four years ago to 1,200 locations across the United States today." The key N2 vocabulary-and-grammar pattern「Noun ＋ を売り物にする」(in its shortened form,「N ＋ を売り物に」) means "to make something a selling point or attractive feature." It is commonly used with nouns in business and commercial contexts to emphasize a marketing strategy aimed at widespread consumer needs. In an N2 reading question asking for a reason (理由), connect the expansion (「またたく間に広まった」) directly with the benefit received by customers, while watching for traps such as the added word「新型」(new type) in choice (c) or the substitution of「行政」(government administration) as the supervising body in choice (b). The growth was fundamentally driven by patients' practical need for a medical service that was both less time-consuming and cheaper than a general hospital, making choice (a) correct.
default.q.test-20-q1-1.why.0: ✓ (a) This is correct because the passage states that the clinic promotes the advantages of being “fast and inexpensive” (「早い、安い」を売り物に) for patients who dislike waiting at ordinary hospitals, and that it consequently expanded throughout the country.
default.q.test-20-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) Incorrect because the text mentions only a simple system, such as supervision by an internist. It does not mention an administrative organization, nor is this the reason the clinic attracts patients and becomes extremely busy.
default.q.test-20-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) Incorrect because the article only discusses the usual seasonal flu vaccine, not a vaccine for a new strain (新型). In addition, vaccine availability occurred only at some clinics, so it cannot represent the cause of the increase throughout the United States.
default.q.test-20-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) Incorrect because the passage does not mention that the large chains have built trust. On the contrary, it quotes doctors criticizing them for opening clinics solely for profit and expressing concern about overprescribing medication.
default.q.test-27-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) Aは、対人コミュニケーションについて、Bは恋愛心理学について述べている。
The concluding sentence of passage A emphasizes applying the psychology of habits to communication between people (対人コミュニケーション), while the concluding sentence of passage B focuses on applying it to the psychology of love (恋愛心理).
default.q.test-27-q1-1.explanation: In passage A, the key N2 grammar is the formal noun pattern 「～において」, meaning “in / within,” used in 「対人コミュニケーションにおいて」 (in interpersonal communication). The final sentence of passage A states: 「このような癖を応用した心理学は対人コミュニケーションにおいて様々な活用ができるといえよう」 (It can be said that psychology applying these habits can be used in various ways in interpersonal communication). The final sentence of passage B states: 「これを恋愛心理に応用することもできるのだ」 (It can also be applied to romantic psychology). These sentences clearly identify the respective scopes of application. Learners may be misled by choice (b) because both passages mention deception (「嘘をついていたり」 and 「虚偽の出来事」), but passage A also discusses telling the truth (「正直に話している」), so detecting lies is merely an illustrative example, not the overall purpose. In N2 comparative reading questions, avoid options focusing on isolated details and follow the concluding, directional sentences of each passage: passage A concerns social communication in general, while passage B narrows the focus to romantic relationships.
default.q.test-27-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) This is incorrect because both passages discuss temporary psychological states through unconscious habits, rather than analyzing the other person's personality (人格).
default.q.test-27-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) Incorrect because Passage A analyzes both gestures when telling the truth and gestures when lying through eye direction; it is not only about lying behavior.
default.q.test-27-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) This is incorrect because Passage A does not discuss personality (性格), while Passage B explains touching one’s nose as a reflex used to conceal deception, not as an expression of intimacy (親密感).
default.q.test-27-q1-1.why.3: ✓ (d) This is correct because the concluding sentence of passage A states that the application is used in communication between people (対人コミュニケーション), while passage B states that it is used in the psychology of love (恋愛心理).
default.q.test-45-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) 代表取締役社長が亡くなったので会社をさらに応援してほしいということ
The letter both announces the death of the representative director and serves as a formal message to business partners expressing the company’s wish for their continued support and cooperation in the future.
default.q.test-45-q1-1.explanation: Based on the passage, the central message is conveyed by the announcement 「かねてから療養中でありました弊社 代表取締役 社長 松竹梅男（九十歳）が永眠いたしました」 together with the request 「今後とも変わらぬご指導ご鞭撻のほどよろしくお願いいたします」. The complete request means: "We sincerely hope that we may continue to receive your guidance and encouragement in the future." In terms of usage, 「ご指導ご鞭撻」 combined with the indirect, polite request pattern 「N + のほどよろしくお願いいたします」 is common in business contexts when expressing a desire for continued support and guidance from business partners. Do not confuse it with the formal seasonal greeting at the end, 「向寒の折から...」. Also note that 「お心遣い」 refers to condolences or consideration shown at a funeral, not to a New Year's greeting card, 「年賀状」.
default.q.test-45-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The seasonal health wish at the end of the letter is merely a conventional greeting in business writing, not the main purpose.
default.q.test-45-q1-1.why.1: ✓ (b) The sender announces the director’s death and asks the business partner to continue looking after, working with, and supporting the company in the years ahead.
default.q.test-45-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) The letter only asks permission to decline condolence gifts or offerings (お心遣い); it does not mention declining New Year’s cards (年賀状) at all.
default.q.test-45-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) The passage does not mention appointing a new director or requiring the partner to give strict instructions to anyone.
default.q.test-45-q15-15.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) Someone who independently enjoys facilities such as tourist attractions and theme parks, where group use is common
In the passage, 「お一人様」 refers to people who independently enjoy life and willingly use entertainment and travel services that are usually intended for groups or families.
default.q.test-45-q15-15.explanation: From a vocabulary perspective, 「お一人様」(おひとりさま) originally comes from honorific language used in the service industry: the polite prefix 「お」 combines with the noun 「一人」 and the respectful suffix 「様」, which is used to address a customer dining or traveling alone. It has a positive nuance, describing the independent lifestyle of people who actively enjoy leisure and social activities by themselves. The direct basis is found in passage A: 「趣味やプライベートを一人で楽しんだり、住居や老後の準備を行うなど自立した一人の人間として生きる「お一人様」の人もいれば、やむを得ず「お一人様」の人もいるだろう。」 and passage B: 「旅行、食事、映画など現在では「お一人様」を対象にしたサービスも各社、積極的に展開している。」 Together, these mean: “Some people are ‘solo customers’ who live as independent individuals, enjoying their hobbies and private lives alone and preparing for their housing and retirement, while others are ‘solo customers’ out of necessity... Today, companies are also actively expanding services aimed at people who travel, dine, or watch movies alone.” Be careful of distractor (a), which contains the extreme absolute expression 「どんなことでも」 (“anything whatsoever”), a phrase not found in the passage. Choice (b) most accurately reflects the nature of 「お一人様」 in modern society.
default.q.test-45-q15-15.why.0: ✗ (a) This is incorrect because the passage never states that the person can independently judge and act in every situation (どんなことでも).
default.q.test-45-q15-15.why.1: ✓ (b) This is correct because the passage clearly states that「お一人様」refers to people who enjoy personal interests by themselves and use services that are usually associated with groups, such as travel, dining, and watching movies.
default.q.test-45-q15-15.why.2: ✗ (c) The content refers only to people living alone or remaining unmarried (独身世帯, 未婚); it does not mention spouses living apart because one of them is working away from home (単身赴任).
default.q.test-45-q15-15.why.3: ✗ (d) The reason for not getting married in the passage is valuing freedom and not having found a suitable partner, not lacking friends or having difficulty communicating with others.
default.q.test-46-q13-13.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 「子供としての自分」を経験している段階
The key point is that, according to the author, understanding one’s parents’ feelings from the past means experiencing “oneself as a child” (「子供としての自分」を経験している). This belongs to the deeper knowledge gained through experience, not to “experiencing being a parent” (親を体験している), which refers only to having children and fulfilling the practical parental role.
default.q.test-46-q13-13.explanation: The underlined expression uses the key N2 grammar pattern 〜に過ぎない, combined with the plain form of a verb or a noun. Here, it is 親を体験している + に過ぎない, meaning “it is merely / nothing more than...” and emphasizing that something remains at a basic, superficial level rather than representing deeper understanding. The complete sentence means: “However, at this stage, it is merely an experience of being a parent.” The relevant passage is: 「これは、時を経てから、「子供としての自分」を経験していることになる。子供を体験して大人になり、親を体験しながら「子供を経験」する。」 For this type of question, distinguish the two contrasts established by the author: 体験 (an outward, firsthand experience) versus 経験 (knowledge gained through experience), and 親 (parent) versus 子供 (child). The author states that understanding a parent’s feelings is an accumulation of insight for one’s former self as a child (「子供としての自分」を経験している), not the essential meaning of experiencing the role of a parent (親を体験している). Therefore, choice (c) does not match the definition of the underlined expression.
default.q.test-46-q13-13.why.0: ✗ (a) Incorrect because the author clearly states that marriage and having children only constitute direct personal experience, which exactly matches the meaning of “the experience of being a parent.”
default.q.test-46-q13-13.why.1: ✗ (b) Understanding the feelings involved in raising children is a psychological process that occurs alongside the experience of becoming a parent (親を体験しながら).
default.q.test-46-q13-13.why.2: ✓ (c) This is correct because the passage states that the person is “experiencing oneself as a child” (「子供としての自分」を経験している), not “experiencing being a parent” (親を体験している).
default.q.test-46-q13-13.why.3: ✗ (d) Understanding one's children's feelings is connected to parents' growing awareness through the experience of raising them; it is not an option that contrasts with the nature of the object, as (c) does.
default.q.test-46-q21-21.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) 一緒に住んでいるお兄さんが代理に行く場合、委任状を作成しなければならない。
For the certificate-issuance procedure, a person acting on someone else’s behalf—including an older brother who lives with them—is not automatically recognized as an authorized representative and must have a letter of authorization under administrative regulations.
default.q.test-46-q21-21.explanation: The question asks for the correct explanation of the procedure for obtaining a certificate of entries in the foreign resident registration record. Option (b) means: "If an older brother living in the same household completes the procedure on the person's behalf, a letter of authorization must be prepared." The grammar pattern `～なければならない` expresses a mandatory rule or legal obligation. The passage clearly states: 「【交付申請場所】・区役所区民課外国人登録係又は各事務所の戸籍住民係 (郵送による交付申請は受け付けておりません) 【手数料】・1通300円」. Unlike the earlier procedures for new registration or a lost card, which allow a cohabiting relative to act on behalf of a person under 16, this certificate application has no such exception; a representative must have a letter of authorization. In administrative-information questions, note the exclusion clues: 「1通300円」 means everyone must pay the fee, eliminating (a), and 「(郵送による交付申請は受け付けておりません)」 rules out applying for and receiving it by mail, eliminating (d).
default.q.test-46-q21-21.why.0: ✗ (a) This choice is incorrect because the document specifies a fixed fee of 300 yen per copy (1通300円) and contains no provision for a fee waiver when the applicant applies in person.
default.q.test-46-q21-21.why.1: ✓ (b) This choice is correct because when someone else handles an administrative document procedure on your behalf, a valid letter of authorization is required.
default.q.test-46-q21-21.why.2: ✗ (c) This choice is incorrect because the content concerns the procedure for losing a foreign resident registration card, not the certificate application requested in the sentence.
default.q.test-46-q21-21.why.3: ✗ (d) This choice is incorrect because the passage clearly states that the committee does not accept applications for issuance by mail (郵送による交付申請は受け付けておりません).
